# Test fixtures

Generated by [`make-fixtures.sh`](make-fixtures.sh) using `sfdisk`, `sgdisk`,
`mkfs.vfat`, `mkfs.exfat` and `mtools` — real tools writing real images, never
hand-crafted bytes. No root required: everything happens on plain files.

```bash
./tests/fixtures/make-fixtures.sh
```

Images land in `gen/`, which is gitignored. Tests skip cleanly when it is absent.

## Ground truth

Every value below was read out of the images with `python3`/`xxd`/`sgdisk`, **not**
with blktamper. That is the point: a test asserting what our own parser produced
proves only that the parser is consistent with itself. Use these numbers when
writing assertions.

- partition 0: type `0x0C`, status `0x80`, start LBA 2048, 129024 sectors

## Deliberately broken fixtures

| Image | What is wrong | What it exercises |
|---|---|---|
| `gpt-badcrc.img` | primary header CRC32 overwritten with `DE AD BE EF` | stored-vs-computed display; primary/backup divergence |
| `garbage.img` | 1 MiB of random bytes | no probe may claim it; forcing an interpretation must not panic |
| `zeros.img` | 1 MiB of zeros | the same, for the other degenerate input |

## A note on `mkfs.vfat` sizes

Its `BLOCKS` argument counts **1 KiB blocks, not sectors**. Passing a sector count
silently produces a filesystem claiming twice the space, which then overruns both
its partition and the image. The generator divides by two and the values above
confirm `total_sectors_32` (129024) now matches the partition exactly.

This bit once already — worth keeping in mind before adding a fixture.

## The residue fixture

`mbr-fat32.img` exists to exercise the question blktamper is for: what survives a
delete? Two files are created and then removed with `mdel`:

- `/SECRET.TXT` — its directory entry survives as a `0xE5` tombstone with the first
  filename character destroyed, readable at root entry `[6]` as `.ECRET  TXT`.
- `/a-long-directory-name/deleted-payload.bin` — the same, one directory down, and
  large enough that its cluster chain is worth following.

Both files' data clusters are untouched by `mdel`. A FAT reader that hides deleted
entries the way a filesystem driver does would show neither, which is precisely the
behaviour this tool exists not to have.
